p3c1.opener_idea: GRAND weight (626 paras): full-bleed plate band, composition split by the ray screen itself -- upper register shows the false image (mountain top / empty sky with faint shimmer strips), lower register the true valley (gold dollar beacon on granite column, fir pyramids, Stockton smokestack). Dagny's belly-landed plane small in the meadow foreground gives human scale. Kicker SIG III-01; caption names the Terminal line. Why grand: the part's gateway chapter and the reader's first sight of the valley must land as arrival, not illustration.
p3c1.palette_role: First valley-light intrusion on the red part: earned CLEAR GREEN intruder (documented exception per draft grammar) -- green leaves, turquoise lake, sunlit grass -- held inside the red part frame. The stop aspect lamp burns red in the kicker while the plate itself is the one green plate in Part III, which is exactly the chapter's meaning: life goes on strike INTO green.
p3c1.proposed_motif: ray-screen valley reveal + gold dollar beacon
p3c1.rationale: Opens with the crash awakening: sunlight, green leaves, Galt's guiltless face [0-14]; her plane lies flat on its belly in the grass [21]. Galt names the valley 'The Taggart Terminal' [22-23] -- the chapter's thesis image, paid off at [594] where the Terminal room is 'the end of track, the point beyond the curve of the earth where the two straight lines of rail met and vanished.' The valley is hidden by a refractor ray screen projecting a false mountaintop [38-50]. Its coat-of-arms is a three-foot solid-gold dollar sign on a granite column, 'its beacon' [72]. Tour beats: turquoise lake [304], Stockton Foundry [376], Midas mint gold coinage [438]. Closes in the anteroom with pencil-cut inscriptions from Wyatt, Danagger, Marsh [622-625].

p3c10.opener_idea: COMPACT weight (327 paras): the quiet coda plate -- a single motionless headlight beam going 'off into a limitless night' [314], rendered as one flat Headlight wedge over black desert, with the small letters TT on the engine front [313] as the only other element. No dollar, no valley, no flame in the opener -- the chapter EARNS those across its length, and the plate must not spend them in advance. Why compact: per A1 the coda stays quiet; the opener is an exhale, and the closing sequence carries the chapter's visual climax instead.
p3c10.palette_role: Red part resolving: the plate is monochrome beam-on-black; color enters only in the closing body-zone sequence (valley window rectangles in warm Headlight + Wyatt's Torch flame in Stop Red [324] + the traced dollar [326]). The torch flame is the part's last red -- and the book's last image of fire kept, not spent. Green returns exactly once, in the birch-twigs' 'upward thrust' line [316] -- no green artwork, prose only.
p3c10.proposed_motif: the motionless headlight beam + the dollar traced over earth
p3c10.rationale: Opens with Dagny talking her way past the Project F guard [0-14]; the rescue [60-180] ('Price no object' [220]). Then Eddie Willers and the Comet stalled on alien Arizona rail [243-256]: bleeding hands on the motors [265], Division Headquarters dead on the live wire [248-250], 'Don't let it go!' [246,295,310], the rabbit at the Comet's steps [312], the TT letters [313], collapse across the rail under the motionless headlight [314]. The turn: Halley's Fifth streaming over the valley [315]. The window-rectangle sequence -- Mulligan's investments [317], Danneskjold reading Aristotle's law of contradiction [319], Narragansett's new clause [320], Francisco's smelter drawing [321] -- then Wyatt's Torch waving on the earth's edge [324], 'The road is cleared' [325], and the dollar traced over the desolate earth [326].

p3c10.reading_treatment: The chapter's climax lives in the body zone, not the opener: the four window rectangles [317-321] earn a one-chapter device -- each window passage opens with a small flat Headlight rectangle in the margin, four in sequence, like lights coming on down the valley. The final two lines [325-326] set with extra air above; the dollar-tracing line is the book's last sentence and gets no ornament at all -- Phase 2 must not hang an end-mark after it (documented omission; the book ends on the gesture). Drop cap standard.
p3c10.title: IN THE NAME OF THE BEST WITHIN US

p3c2.opener_idea: MONUMENTAL weight (694 paras -- longest in Part III by paragraphs): tallest plate band (13rem) + two-line inscription. Composition: the valley at work in section -- powerhouse, smelter sheets, mine trail, Mulligan house strung like 'a railroad car imbedded in the sky' [383], red breath of Stockton foundry above. The inscription's second line is the blindfold sentence [581] set in Space Mono, forecasting the exit. Why monumental: at 32,088 words this is the part's heaviest sustained read and the utopia must feel built, not sketched.
p3c2.palette_role: Second green-intrusion chapter, warmer than p3c1: smelter amber and foundry red-breath inside the green valley frame. Francisco's copper-mine gold threads through. The red stop lamp stays in the kicker as the outside world's claim on the reader -- the chapter ends by expelling Dagny back into red [686-693].
p3c2.proposed_motif: valley industry at work + blindfold departure
p3c2.rationale: Opens on domestic morning; Galt is called to the powerhouse about the ray screen Dagny's plane knocked off key [0-2]. The chapter's two load-bearing scenes: Francisco's full confession that the playboy was cover for destroying d'Anconia Copper in plain sight [203, read in full], and the lovers' study of his new smelter sheets on the floor [250-251]. Valley economy beats: Mulligan Bank account [97,127], Francisco's valley copper mine [247]. Night passage: valley lights below, 'the red breath of Stockton's foundry above,' Mulligan's windows 'like a railroad car imbedded in the sky' [383]. Closes with the blindfold flight out [676,686] and the plane shrinking 'like a star' over scorched weeds and a crumbled smokestack [693] -- the green-to-rust transition that hands the reader back to the stopped world.

p3c3.opener_idea: GRAND weight (537 paras): the plate is the glass broadcast cage -- a Rearden-Metal microphone stem centered under a hard white beam wedge, control-booth faces as a dark silhouette band above the glass line. The beam is FLAT white (Headlight at full value), no glow filter: it must read as interrogation light, not aura. Kicker SIG III-03; caption cites the off-air line. Why grand: the chapter's center is a set-piece confrontation staged for the whole nation; the opener must feel like walking into the cage.
p3c3.palette_role: Red part, hard-cut: the white beam is the intrusion -- the only full-value white wedge in the cohort, reserved for this chapter's broadcast cage and never reused. Grandstand wood and Iowa dust stay in Railsteel gray so the beam owns the plate. Project X's invisible ray is deliberately NOT pictured (the novel insists it cannot be seen [63]) -- the plate shows only its target: the farmhouse.
p3c3.proposed_motif: Rearden-Metal microphone in the glass cage under a white beam
p3c3.rationale: Opens with Stadler dragged to the Iowa plain and its three wooden grandstands [0-17]. Project X unveiled: the Xylophone lever panel [59], the invisible sound ray [61-63], the farmhouse target [51], the Thompson Harmonizer naming [63], and the live demolition [68]. The chapter's dramatic center is Dagny's forced appearance on Bertram Scudder's program: 'a beam of white light beating down upon the glittering metal of a microphone -- in the center of a glass cage,' the microphone made of Rearden Metal [427], the booth faces watching from above [428]. Her defiant confession speech [434-441] ends with the station cut off -- 'due to technical difficulties' [447] -- and the taxi driver's 'Thank you, ma'am' [448]. Closes in Rearden's apartment: 'does such a place really exist?' [527] and the void of the unfoundable man [536].

p3c4.opener_idea: STANDARD weight (499 paras -- just under the grand threshold, and the quiet is the point): a narrow plate -- the parapet line dead-center, black river-and-sky void below, the distant calendar page floating above the roofs. No lamp glow; the calendar numerals are the only lit element, set in flat blood-red. Why standard: this is the part's intimate horror chapter (a marriage, a night walk, a suicide); a grand plate would monumentalize what the prose keeps unbearably close.
p3c4.palette_role: Red part at its darkest: orange-haze twilight [2] is the intrusion -- a sickly amber-orange reserved for Jim Taggart's chapters, distinct from Part II's Order Amber (document and keep separate at conformance: Taggart-haze vs. caution-amber). The calendar's 'letters of blood' [479] are the chapter's single saturated red inside the plate.
p3c4.proposed_motif: the calendar in letters of blood + the parapet over black water
p3c4.rationale: Opens with Jim Taggart dropping a $100 bill into a beggar's indifferent hand [0-2] under orange-haze twilight. The day's deals (Argentina/Chile loans, Interneighborly Amity [5-9]) frame the Jim/Cherryl anniversary thread [115]. The chapter's heart is Cherryl's visit to Dagny: the wedding apology [242-244], 'I married Jim because I thought he was you' [244], 'We're sisters, aren't we?' [249-250], and her admission that she no longer wishes to fight [283]. Closes with Cherryl's night walk: the calendar reading September 2 'in letters of blood' [479], the signal passage -- 'no signals ... no way to tell destruction from safety, or enemy from friend' [493] -- and her run over the parapet into the river [495-498]. The 'no signals' line makes this the part's dark mirror of p3c5's lantern chapter.

p3c4.reading_treatment: No drop-cap flourish -- a plain cap, deliberately unadorned; this chapter refuses ornament. The Cherryl/Dagny dialogue [242-293] keeps maximum calm measure. End-mark: none. The chapter ends mid-void [498]; Phase 2 should confirm a deliberate absent end-mark (documented omission, not oversight) -- the only chapter in the cohort so treated.
p3c4.title: ANTI-LIFE

p3c5.opener_idea: GRAND weight by documented boundary exception (500 paras = the scale threshold; content earns the step up): the catastrophe plate. Composition: Tower A as a 'lighted glass cube ... like a crown without a body' [387] centered over a fan of dead tracks; signal lenses rendered as dead glass eyes [338]; a single red lantern flame held aloft at the vanishing point -- Galt's lantern [498]. Why grand despite the count: this is the part's hinge -- the stop made physical -- and the opener must carry the most complex scene in the cohort (tower + dead signals + lantern) without crowding.
p3c5.palette_role: The red-part core: Stop Red owns this plate outright -- dead red lenses, the red lantern, the funeral-pyre glow of the docks. No intrusion color at all; this chapter IS the aspect. Wheat-gold appears only inside the body-zone treatment (below), never in the plate, so the opener stays pure stop.
p3c5.proposed_motif: dead signal lenses + the red lantern held against midnight
p3c5.rationale: Opens with the breaking copper wire in California [0-1] and the September 2 calendar [5]. Dagny reads the Taggart map's 'red arteries' [7]. Twin destructions: the d'Anconia docks blown up on the stroke of the nationalization vote [86-89], its glare in every New York face as a 'funeral pyre' [97]; and the Minnesota wheat catastrophe -- trains 193/194 [8-10], the broken elevator wire [294], the flood of wheat [295-296], cars diverted to Kip's Ma's soybeans [326], wheat rotting under 'the unchanging green light of signals that called for motion to trains that were not there' [328]. Then the signals themselves die -- 'the dead stare of glass eyes' [338], Tower A hanging 'like a crown without a body' [387] -- and Dagny orders men with lanterns at every post [393-408]. Galt appears as a lamppost till dawn [494]; the closing vision is the red lantern that 'stopped the movement of the world' [498], answered by the bum's 'Who is John Galt?' [499].

p3c6.opener_idea: STANDARD weight (467 paras): the plate is the pour -- a flat furnace-glare wedge sweeping across a dark mill interior, silhouetting a rooftop sentinel figure with two raised pistols [420]. The glare must be FLAT (two stacked wedges, lighter over darker), never a gradient glow: the salute-and-farewell light [466] rendered as lithograph slabs. Why standard: a long chapter but a single-arc one (siege -> quit -> reveal -> pour); the plate needs force, not height.
p3c6.palette_role: Red part with the furnace intrusion: pour-orange/red glare reserved for this chapter and distinct from both Taggart-haze (p3c4) and Order Amber (Part II) -- three warm hues that Phase 2 must keep spectrally separated (document exact hexes at conformance). The gold bar from the 'gold-haired pirate' [10] appears only as a caption reference, never pictured -- gold discipline holds: no gilt in the plate.
p3c6.proposed_motif: furnace pour glare + the two-gun rooftop sentinel
p3c6.rationale: Opens on the dated siege diary: Oct 20 wage demand [0], tuyeres knocked off the blast furnace [5], the fraudulent attachment notice [7] -- answered by the gold bar in Rearden's safe [10] and the Wayne-Falkland summons [12]. Verified: ZERO music terms in the chapter text -- 'concerto' is purely metaphorical (deliverance orchestrated), so no instrument or score imagery is grounded; the deliverance is Rearden's quitting plus Francisco's reveal. Beats: 'Who is the guiltiest man in this room?' answered 'I am' [335]; Francisco on the gatehouse roof firing two guns 'like a hero of Western legend' [420]; the reveal -- soot-streaked, in scorched overalls -- 'I was your furnace foreman' [445-455]. Closes with the pour: 'The glare of steel being poured from a furnace shot to the sky,' the red glow sweeping the office 'as if in salute and farewell' [466].

p3c7.opener_idea: STANDARD plate + the LONG-ADDRESS APPARATUS (396 paras but 37,525 words -- densest in the library): the plate is small and grave -- a dead radio dial at 7:51 beside an empty television screen [107], the voice-without-face. All design weight goes to the apparatus, not the hero (per A1): (1) movement numerals in Space Mono at the nine speech movements, keyed to real paragraph indices; (2) a thin progress spine in the margin tracking movements I-IX; (3) relief spacing before each movement head. Why standard plate: a bigger hero would lie about where the chapter's weight sits -- it sits in the 60 pages of speech, and the design must serve the reading, not the arrival.
p3c7.palette_role: Red part, voice register: the plate is near-monochrome Railsteel -- dead dial, empty screen, gray studio -- with ONE red element: the clock hand at 8:00 [102]. The speech body zone stays calm Headlight; movement numerals in Stop Red carry the part color through the long read without tinting a single word of prose.
p3c7.proposed_motif: the dead dial at 7:51 + the voice without a face
p3c7.rationale: Opens with Rearden gone -- 'He's gone!' [2-8]. The Thompson broadcast buildup [32-39] (billboards, sky-writing, square loud-speakers) sets up the hijack: music dies at 7:51 [71], every station in the country dead with equipment in perfect order [90], a wall of unknown radio waves from an impossible transmitter [93-94], the clock reaching 8:00 [102], then 'Mr. Thompson will not speak to you tonight' [103] and 'This is John Galt speaking' [106] -- voice only, screen empty [107]. Speech movements mapped by full para-index scan: I. Strike declaration [108-119]; II. Life/morality standard [120-149]; III. Axioms: existence, identity, A is A [150-167]; IV. Virtues: independence through pride [168-175]; V. Trader/force [181-190]; VI. Sacrifice dissected [210-247]; VII. Mystics/savages/causality [250-312]; VIII. Autobiography: the motor, the factory meeting, the quit [313-319]; IX. The middle is evil [344], rights/government [370-373], the machine [379], return + oath [388-395]. Closes with the oath [395].

p3c8.opener_idea: MONUMENTAL weight (729 paras -- longest in the part by paragraphs): the banquet plate -- a long speakers' table in flat silhouette under a 'cobweb of dead microphones' [5], the television screen's 'tensely bluish light' [710] as a flat rectangle above, and at its center the small standing figure with the momentarily EXPOSED gun [728]. Why monumental: the chapter stages the part's most crowded set pieces (studio, manhunt, arrest, interrogation, banquet) and the opener must read as a full stage, not a vignette.
p3c8.palette_role: Red part, gray register: 'a spread of gray sky' [680] is the intrusion -- cold broadcast-studio gray, the color of the dead microphones, the empty screen, the window sill confrontation. The exposed gun [728] gets the plate's single Stop Red accent (muzzle-face dot). The 'bluish light' of the TV screen [710] is rendered as flat slate, never glow.
p3c8.proposed_motif: the window-sill figure + the exposed gun on live television
p3c8.rationale: Opens in the studio aftermath: the radio reduced to 'a wooden box with some knobs' [1], the deserted drawing room 'under a cobweb of dead microphones' [5]. Official broadcasts deny and co-opt the speech [157-181], including the secret short-wave 'Calling John Galt!' [181]. Dagny searches the Terminal tunnels night after night [221]; Galt warns her the arrest is half an hour away and orders her to play his enemy [242-247]. The arrest [304-323]; Thompson's interrogations; Dagny's $500,000 reward check fluttering to her desk [583]. Stadler's confrontation with Galt sitting on the window sill 'against a spread of gray sky' [680-683]. Closes at the banquet: the TV screen's bluish rectangle [710], Mouch's 'John Galt Plan' [724], and Galt rising with the gun 'momentarily exposed to the sight of the world' -- 'Get the hell out of my way!' [728].

p3c9.opener_idea: COMPACT weight (264 paras -- shortest in the part): a low, wide plate -- the Project F concrete cube [170-171] (asymmetric cubes, single slit window like 'a face with a single eye') sunk in black trees, one red dial-dot lit in the dark. Nothing more. Why compact: the chapter is a night raid and a cellar; compression IS the atmosphere. A tall plate would ventilate what the prose seals shut.
p3c9.palette_role: Red part at blackest: concrete gray + dial red on near-Tunnelblack. The Xylophone/celebration reds of p3c3 return here as instrument reds -- dial segments, the red glass button [174] -- deliberately rhyming p3c3's panel with p3c9's cabinet (documented rhyme: the looters' two machines share one red). The 100-mile destruction circle [92] is never pictured -- only its rim light on the horizon line of the plate.
p3c9.proposed_motif: the concrete cube with one eye + the dead generator beside the living one
p3c9.rationale: Opens with Stadler hearing 'Get the hell out of my way!' on his car radio before it dies [0-2], then the night drive across Iowa behind 'two small signals of danger' (his own taillights) [4]. The mushroom dome [7,15], the broken fence and body by the shanty [13-14], the Friends of the People seizing Project X to found 'Meigsville' [42-47]. Project X turns on itself: the structure rises silently and comes down as rubble, the 100-mile circle wiped out [92]; the Taggart Bridge gone [159]. Then Project F: the concrete cube on the Institute hill [170-171], the cellar room under 'naked rock' [172], the Persuader cabinet with its dials, red segments, and single red button [174]. The torture: heartbeat on the amplifier [179], shocks [181-201], the generator dying -- drone and heartbeat ceasing together [212-214] -- Galt's engineer's repair instructions [232], Taggart's breaking [248-257]. Closes: 'the cellar where the living generator was left tied by the side of the dead one' [263].

direction_chosen: STOP-AND-PROCEED: the cohort composes within the draft signal-plate grammar (Direction A 'THE SIGNAL': Part III = red/stop-and-proceed aspect, flat night-lithograph SVG) as the STOP movement. Compositional constant across all ten openers: a horizontal stop-register -- a dead-aspect band (dead lenses, dead dials, dead wires, parapet line, concrete horizon) sitting low in every plate -- while each chapter's scene above it is fully authored from its own prose. The two valley chapters break the register with green (documented intruders); the three flame chapters answer it with held red (lantern, pour, torch); the speech chapter shrinks the plate and spends its weight on the reading apparatus instead. This keeps the draft grammar's part-aspect system, its flat industrial medium, its gold refusal (no gilt anywhere in the cohort -- Midas gold appears only as caption text), and its F7/F8 cleanliness (every variation authored per chapter, this map is the documentation). Nothing here finalizes tokens, type, or SVG -- Phase 2 re-keys to the broadcast ART-DIRECTION.md.
direction_rejected: REJECTED 1 -- 'THE XYLOPHONE': every opener as a control-panel strip (dials, levers, buttons) keyed to chapter events. Rejected because: (a) the panel conceit fits the looters' chapters but trivializes the valley and cannot hold the 37,525-word speech with any gravity; (b) ten panel strips risk the exact repeated-ornament failure the benchmark bans; (c) panels read as UI chrome, not authored scenes -- the title-swap test fails. REJECTED 2 -- 'TWO WORLDS SPLIT': every opener split down the middle -- stopped world left, valley right. Rejected because: (a) it literalizes the theme into a repetitive diptych; (b) it fails title-swap; (c) at phone widths the halves collapse into illegible slivers; (d) several chapters have no valley half, forcing invented content.
